acceptance.criterion: A repeatable benchmark command with frozen inputs (the plan's case list), recorded versions, lock files, and input checksums.

A local baseline table: phase costs (validation, preparation, CSR assembly, passModel, each stage, pool solves, result checks), model rows, columns, and nonzeros, total time, and memory, for every frozen case.
The pinned highs runtime is checked by calls, not types, for row addition and deletion, objective and row-bound changes, option reset, zeroAllClocks, and a MIP start; the result decides B4.
Vercel feasibility in turflp-bench: the example route deployed, worker_threads, WASM loading, and worker termination proved or disproved, and the B6 execution path selected.
The latency budget and memory and queue caps are set from the measurements.
An internal immutable prepared representation is reused across sizes and the default minimum cover; fixed-specific state is separate and never mutates the original sets.
Bitset operations pass boundary tests at 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, and 65 respondents, empty sets, and complements.
Packed and original calculations agree; input order and public validation are unchanged; memory is bounded.
A WASM 64-bit kernel is measured against the JS kernel; the retained kernel improves a measured workload, or the change is recorded as rejected.
docs/algorithm.md documents the fixed-cover removal and the weighted residual groups, with the proof of exactness and the covered and uncovered bound rules.
Reduced and original models agree with the exhaustive oracle and the conformance suite of all ports, with the reduction on and off.

The plan's regression fixtures pass, including unequal weights, unreachable respondents, fixed products covering everyone, a needed candidate with zero residual reach, residual twins with different original reach, and the pinned unique optima.
Minimum cover and default sizes agree; the empty-residual model is valid; a false constant bound is infeasible.
The skip-a-solve checks (John's additions) are measured and kept or rejected.
The retained reduction passes the performance gate, or it is restricted to the workloads where it passes.
One native model per size job holds stage bounds and cuts; the penetration fallback never inherits pool-only rows; models are disposed on success and failure.

Tests cover option and clock resets (finite to unlimited, decreasing limits, repeated solves), first-stage failure, fallback, zero pool budget, timed pool exhaustion, presolve on and off, and different fixed sets.
The greedy MIP start is measured and kept or rejected.
Retained reuse lowers measured total time.
The dashboard uses the same preparation and reduction rules, with distinct names for group count, reachable count, and respondent count.
Dashboard analysis and package results agree; weighted frontier and tie-count fixtures pass; contributions sum to the original reach.
typecheck, test, build, and test:browser pass in both browser modes, with the fixed-change-during-run, sort, filter, and focus behavior kept.
Preparation is per run, cancellation and the queued cover work, and no buffer the UI uses is detached.
fixed works through HTTP; malformed input and limits give 400, 413, 429 or 503, 504, and 500 as stated.
Solves run off the request thread; a whole-job deadline terminates a worker, and no capacity is lost after a timeout or crash.
The deployed example in turflp-bench meets the latency and resource budget of B1.
The durable-job and tenant parts are built as John decides, or recorded as an issue.
A measured decision to keep WASM or use native HiGHS for named job classes, or B7 is skipped with its measured reason.
README.md, js/README.md, python/README.md, dashboard/README.md, js/examples/nextjs/README.md, NEWS.md, and docs/algorithm.md match the code.
Version 0.4.0 in DESCRIPTION, python/pyproject.toml, python/uv.lock, python/src/turflp/__init__.py, js and dashboard package.json and package-lock.json, and README examples.

master_acceptance.criterion: turf-astra, turf-grok, and turf-agy report no blocking finding on the cumulative diff at the final head.
Every documented local gate passes on the final head, the Next.js standalone check and the new HTTP and benchmark commands included.
Every GitHub Actions check on the exact final head is green.
The PR is merged with a merge commit; release v0.4.0 is published on that commit with turflp-dashboard.html; PyPI has turfLP 0.4.0.
turf.aigora.ai serves the build of the release (same index.html digest).
